slides.caption: Author → execute → target · artifacts fan out after the run.
slides.lede: The atlas starts at product boundaries. `aiperf` from `aiperf-cli` authors Config v2, re-execs itself as `--execute`, and optionally launches `--cell` children. Load targets are real servers, `aiperf-mock-server`, or in-process Dynosim.
slides.narration: The atlas opens at product boundaries. One aiperf binary authors the run, re-executes itself to dispatch load, and targets a real server, the mock server, or Dynosim.
points: Mock server is a separate target; Dynosim is a transport feature, not a command.

slides.caption: cli → runtime → loadgen-core · mock-server is peer, not child.
slides.lede: Compile-time capability flows `aiperf-cli` → `aiperf-runtime` → `loadgen-core`. The entry process and its `--execute` child share one binary; `aiperf-mock-server` links runtime independently; `pyext` and `e2e` stay off the hot path.

points: Workspace members: loadgen-core, runtime, cli, mock-server, e2e, pyext.
Solid edges are Cargo deps or self re-exec; dashed edges are network or optional features.

slides.caption: stdin: one envelope · stdout: one terminal · parent stays the shell.
slides.lede: Profile resolves `current_exe()`, spawns `aiperf --execute`, writes one strict protocol-v2 envelope to stdin, and waits for exactly one terminal JSONL line on stdout. stderr stays diagnostics-only.
slides.narration: Protocol version two is a fresh process boundary: parent writes one envelope to stdin and reads one terminal JSONL line from stdout.

HTTP and gRPC share identity, prepare different bindings.

slides.caption: hot-path events · post-drain merge · durable report + fan-out.
slides.lede: Transports emit RequestObserver events; worker-local collectors and metrics observers accumulate exact rows or t-digest sketches. After drain, MetricsAccumulator merges stores, joins side channels, commits the report, and exporters fan out.
slides.narration: Measurement is an observer event stream. Workers accumulate locally, merge after drain, join side channels, and exporters fan out from the committed report.

slides.caption: promote → slice → ordinary execute → merge → one commit.
slides.lede: `cells > 1` promotes the execute child into a controller. Cells fetch sliced envelopes over Velo, run the ordinary engine, and return records or folded stores. Optional aggregators merge subtrees; the controller commits once.
slides.narration: Cellular mode promotes the execute child into a controller. Cells run ordinary execute on sliced envelopes and return mergeable partitions over Velo.
points: SLURM and Kubernetes launchers reuse the same controller/cell model.

slides.caption: Cargo features freeze the implementation universe.
slides.lede: Default `aiperf-cli` enables `grpc` and `cellular`. Orthogonal features add `parquet`, `dynosim`, `pyo3-embed`, and `search-pyo3`. `full` unions dynosim + parquet + cellular + grpc. Missing capabilities fail closed at validation.
slides.narration: Cargo features define the linked universe. Default builds include gRPC and cellular; parquet, dynosim, and pyo3-embed opt in and fail closed when missing.
points: Dynosim pulls the pinned Dynamo mocker git dep when the feature is on.
No runtime plugin discovery—capabilities are statically linked factories.

slides.caption: compile-time composition · Clock/Sink substitution · cellular wraps the core.
slides.lede: AIPerfExtension registers datasets, endpoints, transports, workloads, and exporters into a frozen AIPerfRegistry. Execution substitutes Clock and RequestSink implementations; cellular mode scales by wrapping the same single-run core.
slides.narration: The open seams are AIPerfExtension registration at bootstrap and Clock plus RequestSink substitution on the hot path. Cellular wraps that same core.
points: Workloads resolve an execution factory from the prepared transport—no pair matrix.
